reasons.order: Sections build strictly: scope fix, then the reconciliation skip it enables, then the fire-time re-resolution that skip requires, then the shared-store consequence, environment exclusion, and finally the new test — each depends on the one before it.
reasons.why: Each heading states the mechanical cause, e.g. 'the joined string never matched an id the store would ever see', naming the specific mismatch rather than describing the code change alone.
reasons.load: Every claim (scope, skip check, fire-time lookup, conflict behavior, environments exclusion, test contents) has its own diff citation immediately below it, so a reader never has to hold an unverified claim in mind.
reasons.trust: The description of the browser test ('a second asserting that a graph update re-registers only the changed binding while the kept binding still runs the current action') matches the two `test(...)` bodies in plugin.browser.test.ts exactly.

reasons.order: Same build-up as the strongest document: scope fix, skip-reregistration, fire-time resolution, conflict-store change, environment exclusion, then the browser test that exercises all of it.
reasons.why: Good but slightly weaker than a comparable passage: 'that closure can no longer capture the graph node directly — the node it captured may be stale' restates the mechanism without naming why staleness specifically matters (a graph rebuild replaces the action's data closure).
reasons.load: The sentence 'Because an unchanged binding now keeps the closure it was registered with, that closure can no longer capture the graph node directly' requires a re-read to parse the causal chain before the diff resolves it.
reasons.trust: Every factual claim, including the N-way hotkey conflict and the test's use of a versioned graph action, is directly supported by the diff's comments and the test file's `version` atom.

reasons.order: Mostly builds up correctly, but folds two distinct mechanical changes (skip-reregistration and fire-time node resolution) into one heading, weakening the section-per-change structure the other two documents keep.
reasons.why: Explains the N-squared warning blow-up and the stale-closure problem with real causes, matching the changeset's own reasoning about scoped bindings sharing a hotkey.
reasons.load: The 'Skip re-registering an unchanged binding' section makes two separate claims (early-return on match, and node re-resolution at fire time) with no diff block for either, so the reader cannot check them against code in place.
reasons.trust: The 'N-squared blow-up' claim is a reasonable paraphrase of the changeset's 'warns N²/2 times', but stating it as fact with no diff citation for that section leaves it unverifiable within the document itself.
